scenario: The cycle check runs over the rule graph of the compilation unit ([LCYC.3.1]), which is the importer and every library whose rules join its artefact ([LIMP.7.5]). LCYC.8.4, the id, is a tombstone. The library's rule `a` matches X and emits Y; the importer takes both schemas selectively and its rule `b` matches Y and emits X. Neither module has a cycle on its own -- each passes the per-module check in `validate` -- so the only thing that can refuse this is the unit-wide pass (`dsc.cycle.lcyc_6_3_unit_graph`), which keys each schema by its declaring library and so sees `pack`'s X and Y on both sides.
rules_ds:
from pack import X, Y

rule b:
    Y
->
    emit X logical v: 1

libraries.pack:
schema X scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Y scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule a:
    X
->
    emit Y logical v: 1
